title: Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford & Davante Adams discuss injury updates, keys to beating the Bills, limiting penalties & more
headline: Aaron Donald (back), Colby Parkinson, and Jaylen Watson (shoulder) were limited Thursday, with Donald hoped to play Sunday; Myles Garrett's IR window is still undecided.
summary: McVay said Aaron Donald, Colby Parkinson, and Jaylen Watson were limited in Thursday's practice, and that the expectation is they'll be ready if they keep progressing. Donald's back is the main thing to monitor, and McVay said the hope is that he plays Sunday. Parkinson is progressing in a positive direction, and the staff will manage his reps, while Watson will test his shoulder with a harness. Quentin Lake (hip) and Nathan Landman (shoulder) are being managed carefully after heavy snap counts, and McVay called both minor. Myles Garrett is making good progress in rehab, but McVay had not yet decided whether to open his return-to-practice window. Josaiah Stewart was also listed with injuries, and Davante Adams is taking a veteran rest day. McVay also praised Trent McDuffie's consistency and Stafford's leadership, and he discussed penalties, kickoff rule changes, and the Bills matchup.

topics.detail: McVay said the team has had too many flags, mostly from decision making, especially in the kicking game and in scoring position. He wants to fix it without overcorrecting and making players hesitant. Stafford said the offense is hurting itself more than usual, and the penalties affected play-calling in the red zone.
McVay said the new kickoff rules have increased the stakes of late-half situations and created more plays in the kicking game, which has made it a bigger factor.

McVay said Josh Allen is one of the most talented quarterbacks in the NFL, and that the defense will face a big challenge. He also said Buffalo's defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard runs a physical front and disruptive schemes with many pre-snap picture changes.
McVay praised Joe Brady, who was named the league's youngest OC. The Rams signed Eric Kendricks to the practice squad for depth and experience.

McVay said Stafford has been good, but it is still a small sample size. Stafford said he has room to improve and wants to be more consistent, and he feels physically better than this time last season.
